what_i_did: Copied build.py, make_views.py, hero_check.py and run.sh from models/coneflower and reshaped the same design: same origin, orientation, height (0.744 m), meshes (cones, petals, stems, leaves_green, leaves_dark) and material names (Flower_Petal_Pink, Flower_Seed_Orange, Stem_Green, Leaf_Green, Leaf_Dark). No new materials, no variants (plant group).

Scored on the charming hero alone (no turnaround was made). make_views.py keys the cream backdrop and drops the grey-tan cast shadow on the lower left (B/R > 0.6 with G/R 0.8-0.97 in that zone; leaves are olive with B/R < 0.5, petals pink with G/R ~0.6).
hero_check.py unchanged: front-on from 6 deg up, as for the normal model (the charming hero is drawn from the same direction).

9 blooms measured from the charming hero (it has fewer, bigger heads than the normal one's 13), bloom scale 1.42. Each has a plumper 6-sided domed seed cone with an extra rounded crown ring (36 tris) and 7 wide spoon petals, each with a rounded nose point past the tip, drooping 42-55 deg then a further 22 deg.

Stems twice as thick as the normal ones. All leaves are broad ovate cards (6 verts, 4 tris, folded on the midrib) instead of narrow lances: 18 big stem leaves at 30-70 % height and a 40-leaf vase tuft up to 0.52 of the height.

Blooms lean further out from the axis (TILT_OUT 0.9 vs 0.3) and nod more to the camera; the whole clump leans a touch right as it rises (x += 0.04 z^2/H); cones, petals and stems are smooth-shaded; colours a little brighter and more saturated.

979 triangles (budget 1k), 5 meshes, one flat material each, double-sided cards. Height 0.744 m, about 0.58 x 0.38 m in plan (normal: 0.63 x 0.43; width/depth ratio 1.52 vs 1.45). to_game.py coneflower-charming installed simulations/regional-assets-charming/GF-679.glb.
good: Hero silhouette IoU 0.801 at 768 px / 48 samples (normal model: 0.729 on its own hero).
Reads as the same coneflower clump, but chunkier: big orange domes on drooping pink spoon-petal skirts, broad leaves, soft shading.
Same materials and mesh names as the normal model, so seasons and shading roles behave the same.
off: The hero's petals are ~15 thin ragged strips per bloom; at 1k triangles each bloom has 7 wide spoon petals, so skirts read as bells up close.
The hero's leaf mass reaches out to the sides at mid-height; the model's tuft is narrower there (orange slivers on the overlay).
The harness 3/4 'hero' camera does not match a front-on hero and no turnaround exists, so the official harness score is empty (as for the normal model); hero_check.py is the score.
A little cast shadow remains under the front of the clump in views/hero.png (it sits inside the leaf mass, so it barely affects IoU).

rounds.change: Normal build reshaped: 9 blooms from the charming hero, domed 6-sided cones, wide petals, broad 4-tri leaves, thick stems, lean, smooth shading. Blooms too small, tuft too low.
Bloom scale 1.1 -> 1.35, deeper droop, tuft up to 0.52 of the height, longer base leaves.
Looked at it: cones read as balls perched on lampshades. Lower, wider domes, shallower droop with a stronger tip bend, more upright base leaves.
Bloom scale 1.5, bigger stem leaves, softer tip bend.
Bloom scale 1.42, droop 42-55, narrower crown at the ground.
7 spoon petals with a rounded nose instead of 8 square strips (gaps show between petals), base leaves 46 -> 40 to stay under 1k.
Longer stem leaves set higher (30-70 %); final 768 px / 48 samples.

moving_parts: None (plant group: the game poses and sways plants itself).
creative_additions: Rounded spoon-tipped petals and domed seed cones give the toy look; blooms splay outward and the clump leans slightly, so it reads bouncy rather than upright.
